newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds and futures seen subdued by U.S. holiday.
newsitem.headline: Bunds and futures seen subdued by U.S. holiday.

text.p: German Bund futures plotted yet another contract high in early business on Friday but traders said activity was likely to be muted.
With the market becalmed by the July 4 Independence Day holiday in the U.S. and the absence of fundamental data, traders said most business would centre on book-squaring trades ahead of the weekend.

By 0854 GMT the September DTB Bund future was six basis points higher at 102.49, having blipped to a new contract high at 102.52 in early trade. The previous contract high, reached on Thursday, was at 102.46.
In the cash market, the 10-year benchmark Bund was seven basis points higher at 103.02 offering a 5.589 percent bid yield.
Some analysts said the price action over the past few days was a sign that the market was readying itself for a substantial push higher in the coming weeks.

"Bunds are now within a point or so of pushing yields down to new historic lows, and the awareness among domestic investors that they are underweighted and missing out on a significant bull move is growing," Karl Healing of DMG Futures and Options in Frankfurt said in a research note.
Haeling recommended buying on dips and maintaining long positions, particularly at the long end of the market.
The main domestic focus for next week will be June unemlpoyment data, due on Tuesday.
Analysts polled by Reuters expect seasonally-adjusted unemployment to have risen by 20,000 in June.
